newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher on weak yen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished higher on Tuesday as cash stocks with high export exposure rallied after the dollar's sharp rise versus the yen.
Benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract rose 360 points to end at 18,050, 30 points off its intra-day high. Turnover was light at 15,435 lots.
Dealers said continued weakness in banking and construction stocks was eclipsed by gains in export-related issues as the dollar soared to a fresh 50-month high of 126.12 yen in Tokyo.
The U.S. unit was quoted at 125.77/87 yen at 0746 GMT.
Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita's remark that the central bank's monetary policy would continue to focus on ensuring economic recovery reassured players, dealers said.
The remark followed reports that a Japanese government minister had urged the BOJ to consider raising interest rates.
"The fact that the Nikkei couldn't recover further on the back of the strong dollar suggests it won't climb much more. Sentiment is still bad," said a trader with a Japanese house.
He said the June Nikkei was likely to be capped around 18,200, with 17,600 seen as an important support area: "If it breaks 17,600, I think 17,200 will be the next target," he said.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 348.1 against its opening 352.5 as volume hit a new record of 2,525 lots.

Turnover on the Taiwan stock market also reached a new peak of T$238.9 billion as the benchmark index soared to a six-and-a-half year high at the open, but succumbed to individual and institutional profit-taking before the close.

"The fall in the cash index was the first in four days of constant upward moves...as investors still have to be cautious with regard to company results adequately meeting analysts' forecasts," Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary.
